```python
# Simplified Transformer Block (Illustrative)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class SimplifiedTransformerBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, embedding_dim, num_heads):
        super().__init__()
        self.attention = nn.MultiheadAttention(embedding_dim, num_heads)  # Self-attention
        self.linear = nn.Linear(embedding_dim, embedding_dim)
        self.layer_norm1 = nn.LayerNorm(embedding_dim)
        self.layer_norm2 = nn.LayerNorm(embedding_dim)

    def forward(self, x):
        # x: Input tensor (sequence of word embeddings)
        # Residual connection and layer normalization
        x_norm = self.layer_norm1(x)
        attn_output, _ = self.attention(x_norm, x_norm, x_norm)  # Self-attention
        residual = x + attn_output
        x = F.relu(self.linear(residual))
        x = self.layer_norm2(x + x)  # Another residual connection & layer norm
        return x

# Example Usage (Imaginary data)
embedding_dim = 512
num_heads = 8
block = SimplifiedTransformerBlock(embedding_dim, num_heads)
input_tensor = torch.randn(1, 10, embedding_dim)  # Batch size 1, sequence length 10
output_tensor = block(input_tensor)
print(output_tensor.shape) # Should be torch.Size([1, 10, 512])
```

*   **`MultiheadAttention`**:  This is the key. It allows the model to weigh the importance of different words in the input sequence when generating the output. "Multihead" means it performs the attention calculation multiple times with different learned parameters. It calculates how each word relates to every other word in the sequence.
